Many People Are Not Lazy

They Are Just Fighting Battles That Success Has Not Yet Explained

By Raphael OnukuSeptember 16, 20264 minute read

Reflections

← All writing

It has been a while since I wrote a long article on this space. Maybe today is a good day to say something many people feel deeply but may not know how to put into words.

Many people are not lazy. They are just fighting battles that success has not yet explained. They are waking up every day with dreams in their hearts, but also with responsibilities on their shoulders, fear in their minds, and pressure in their pockets.

From a distance, it is easy to judge people. Easy to say someone is not serious. Easy to say someone should have gone farther by now. Easy to ask why they are still struggling, why they have not married, why they have not built, why they have not traveled, why they have not bought land, why they have not become everything people expected.

But life is not as simple as public opinion makes it look. Some people are late because they had to heal first. Some are slow because they had no one to guide them. Some are behind because they started with nothing. Some are quiet because the last disappointment almost broke them.

There are people whose only mistake was being born into families where they had to become adults too early. Before they even understood themselves, life had already placed responsibilities in their hands. They were expected to be strong before they were ready.

There are people carrying family burdens that no one sees. School fees. Hospital bills. House rent. Younger siblings. Aging parents. Unemployed relatives. Emotional wounds. Failed opportunities. Silent fears. Yet when they step outside, the world simply asks why they have not made it yet.

That is why I have learned that before you call someone lazy, first ask what they are carrying. Before you laugh at someone’s small progress, ask what they had to overcome to get there. Before you mock someone’s delay, ask whether you would still be standing if you had lived their story.

But this is also not an excuse to remain in one place forever. Pain may explain your situation, but it should not be allowed to own your future. The fact that life has been hard does not mean you must stop trying. It only means your journey may require more patience, more wisdom, and more discipline.

Sometimes, becoming better begins with one honest conversation with yourself. Not with the world. Not with Facebook. Not with family. Yourself. The kind of conversation where you admit what is hurting you, what is holding you back, what you keep postponing, and what you must finally change.

A person can be tired and still intentional. A person can be wounded and still disciplined. A person can be afraid and still take one step forward. Courage is not always loud. Sometimes, courage is waking up again after a night of private tears and still deciding not to waste the day.

One thing we must stop doing is comparing people’s harvest without knowing their soil. Some people are growing from places of love, support, money, connection, and peace. Others are growing from survival, confusion, rejection, lack, and trauma. The fruits may not appear at the same time.

So if your life is not moving at the speed you imagined, do not insult yourself. Do not turn every delay into self hatred. Do not allow society to convince you that you are nothing because your results are still forming. Some lives are like trees. They spend a long time taking root before anyone sees shade.

But while you are waiting, do not sleep through your own preparation. Learn. Heal. Save what you can. Build your character. Improve your mind. Choose your circle carefully. Stop feeding distractions. Pray if you believe in prayer, but also stand up and do the work that prayer should meet in your hands.

Success is beautiful, but becoming whole is also important. Money is important, but peace is not useless. Achievement is good, but character still matters. The goal is not just to become admired by people. The goal is to become a person you can live with when the noise is gone.

If you read this to the end, I hope you remember that your story is not over because people do not understand your current chapter. Rest when you must, but do not disappear from your own life. Cry if you need to, but do not build a home inside your pain. Start again, even if it is small. One day, what you survived quietly may become the very reason your story will encourage someone else to keep going.
